SMS, MMS and voice: send text messages and place calls from your Twilio numbers.

## API key

- **Get your key here:** [twilio.com](https://www.twilio.com/docs/iam/api-keys/keys-in-console)
- **Settings:** `TWILIO_API_SECRET`, `TWILIO_API_KEY`
- **API reference:** [twilio.com](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/requests-to-twilio)

### Get the key

1. Sign in to Twilio and open [twilio.com](https://www.twilio.com/docs/iam/api-keys/keys-in-console).
2. Create an API key (or token) with only the access your apps need.
3. Copy it. Many providers show a key only once.

**What to create:** A Standard or Restricted API key from Account settings > API keys & auth tokens in the Twilio Console, sent as HTTP Basic (the key's SID and secret); a Standard key can't reach the Accounts or Keys resources. Every path names the account, so the app puts its Account SID in it: /2010-04-01/Accounts/&lt;Account SID>/Messages.json, with a form-encoded body.

Steps for this provider are brief. [Open an issue](https://github.com/every-app/every-app/issues/new?template=provider-request.yml&title=Provider%20guide%3A%20Twilio) to request a full guide.

### Set it on your Gateway

From your EveryApp folder:

```bash
everyapp secret set TWILIO_API_SECRET TWILIO_API_KEY
```

It asks for the value at a hidden prompt, and it's live at once, with no deploy. If an app you've installed needs it, `everyapp configure <app>` asks for it along with everything else the app needs.

### Use it in an app

List it in the app's `everyapp.config.ts`:

```ts
capabilities: {
  twilio: { access: "read", why: "What the app does with it." },
},
```

`access` is `"read"` (or `"write"` where it changes things). The app calls the provider's own URLs with `integrationFetch()`, and the Gateway adds the key. More in [API providers](/docs/agent/providers).

### Check it worked

- `everyapp provider show twilio` shows the key as set and which apps use it.
- `everyapp status` shows apps that were waiting for it as ready.
